references.text: Jesus returned to Cana in Galilee, "where he had turned water into wine." This refers back to the wedding at Cana, where Jesus performed his first sign by turning water into wine ([ref:Joh 2:1-11|John 2:1-11]).
Capernaum is mentioned as a place Jesus went to after the wedding at Cana, and now it is in Capernaum that the royal official's son lies sick ([ref:Joh 2:12|John 2:12]).
The immediate context: Jesus had traveled from Judea to Galilee, and the Galileans welcomed him because they had seen what he did in Jerusalem during the feast ([ref:Joh 4:43-45|John 4:43-45]).
The story of the royal official's sick son continues in the following verses, where Jesus heals the son from a distance ([ref:Joh 4:47-54|John 4:47-54]). This is Jesus' second sign in Galilee.

A parallel account is found in Matthew, where an officer (centurion) in Capernaum asks Jesus to heal his servant, and Jesus heals from a distance through faith ([ref:Matt 8:5-13|Matthew 8:5-13]). Although it may possibly be a different event, the accounts share several common features.

In Luke, there is also an account of an officer in Capernaum who asks for healing for his servant. Although this was likely a different event, it shares features with the royal official's plea in John, especially healing from a distance and faith ([ref:Luk 7:1-10|Luke 7:1-10]).
Natanael from Cana in Galilee is mentioned at the end of the gospel, showing that Cana had a place in the geography of the Gospel of John ([ref:Joh 21:2|John 21:2]).
